children: Crude oil futures fell Monday as traders weighed diplomatic efforts to ease U.S.-Iran hostilities while continued Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia kept concerns alive over Middle East supply risks.

Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey traveled to Tehran for discussions on Monday, with participants reportedly agreeing to continue talks, and Middle Eastern mediators continue to try to revive negotiations between the U.S. and Iran as the Trump administration prepares additional military options.

"Mild optimism about resuming negotiations in the Middle East may help fuel a corrective trend," XS.com senior market analyst Samer Hasn said in a note, adding that he believes "the best the current negotiations could achieve, if they continue, is de-escalation on the Yemen front and an attempt to restore the situation to what it was before the July escalation."

Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said they struck pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West crude oil pipeline and ​Riyadh airport over the weekend, although the attacks still have not been confirmed, and Saudi officials said three drones targeting Riyadh and the country's southern regions were destroyed.

Despite the continuing security risks, oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have recovered substantially, averaging 12.65M bbl/day over seven days, ~25% below the pre-war baseline of 17.15M bbl/day, according to Kpler data reported Friday.

"The market is balancing the bearish signals of a restoration of oil flow from the Middle East and reports of diplomatic Iranian channels remaining open." MST Marquee senior energy analyst Saul Kavonic said in a note, adding that prices could move substantially either way depending on whether the conflict escalates.

At the same time, European natural gas prices rose above €97/MWh for the first time since late 2022, as colder weather threatens to lift demand across the continent while the Iran war continues to disrupt global supplies.
European Union gas storage sites are currently ~75% full, the lowest for the time of year in records going back to 2009, leaving Europe vulnerable to potential disruptions.

European gas prices are still well below the peaks of the last energy crisis in 2022, but the latest advance risks sparking inflation and weighing on economic activity; Europe's LNG imports have lagged last year's levels so far in October despite typically jumping this time of year.
In the U.S., natural gas futures fell as much as 5.4% Monday before settling down 1.4% to the lowest since April, as forecasts shifted significantly warmer over the weekend.
